pages: Tane Mataira, a boy of sixteen, an orange rash vest with black trim down the sides and black board shorts, kneels at the poolside tile with one school exercise book propped on his knee, a pencil against the open leaf. Middle distance: a folded towel, a plastic chair. Background: the big pool, glass doors, morning light.

Marisa Tamati, a woman of thirty-four, dark hair tied back, a navy long-sleeved rash top with a whistle on a lanyard, floats on her back in three metres of water, one long rescue tube held across her chest. Middle distance: the pool wall, lane rope floats. Background: the pool hall windows, ceiling lights on water.

Tane Mataira, a boy of sixteen, an orange rash vest with black trim and black board shorts, floats on his back in the pool with his nose clear of the water, one chrome stopwatch held up in his raised hand. Middle distance: the tiled pool wall, a plastic chair. Background: the pool hall windows, morning light on the water.

Marisa Tamati, a woman of thirty-four, dark hair tied back, a navy long-sleeved rash top with a whistle on a lanyard, crouches at the pool edge holding one folded paper bag open with both hands, the taped seam turned toward her. Middle distance: the steel ladder, a folded towel. Background: the pool hall windows, flat daylight.

Tane Mataira, a boy of sixteen, an orange rash vest with black trim and black board shorts, sits in a plastic chair on the pool deck with his feet in the water, one five-litre rebreather bag on its tube over his mouth and nose.
